drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/check_takes_with_decider.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Decider)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Test whether the decider someone/decider-small can tell a complete take from a cut-short one, using the word-timed transcripts in my transcripts folder."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"check_takes_with_decider":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:check-takes-are-complete-with-a-small-local-model"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/check_takes_with_decider.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.
5. Say plainly to the person that the labels are true by construction (a take as said is usable, one with a controlled fault is not), not real footage.

worked_examples.title: Three takes built from 20 transcripts, two complete and one cut
worked_examples.ask: Can this small model tell a complete take from a cut-off one?
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Decider.test_takes_are_labelled_by_construction_and_scored), run with the test's stand-in decider. transcripts holds 20 files t00..t19, each {"words":[{"text":"This","type":"word"},...]} for "This is sentence number <k> and it has enough words in it to count. Short one." request.json = {"transcripts":"transcripts","model":"someone/decider-small","device":"cpu"}. Run: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/check_takes_with_decider.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"meta":{"n":3,"acc":0.667,"by_kind":{"complete":"2/2","cut":"0/1"},"abstain":{"0.7":{"answered":0,"right":0},"0.8":{"answered":0,"right":0},"0.9":{"answered":0,"right":0}},"ms_per_decision":0},"rows":[{"video":"t8","kind":"complete","usable":true,"take":"This is sentence number 8 and it has enough words in it to count.","p_yes":0.5},{"video":"t0","kind":"complete","usable":true,...},{"video":"t17","kind":"cut","usable":false,"take":"This is sentence number 17 and it","p_yes":0.5}]}}: the stand-in answers 0.5 so it never reaches 0.7 sure (answered 0 at every line); a real decider fills accuracy per fault and how many it gets right when sure.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
